business_problem: Pollinate needed a more scalable and lower-overhead way to ingest financial data and support a multi-tenant banking platform as transaction volumes and merchant onboarding demands outgrew its open-source Kafka setup.
solution_summary: Pollinate adopted Confluent Cloud as the managed event backbone for its banking platform after first outgrowing open-source Kafka and then its Confluent Platform deployment. The architecture now runs as a multi-tenant platform on a single dedicated cluster that handles high-throughput merchant and financial data ingestion while reducing the operational load on an overstretched platform team. Pollinate uses the streaming layer to move data from flat-file ingestion and direct bank integrations into microservices that support onboarding, notifications, and business insights for banking partners and their small-business customers. Real-time streams give banks and merchants visibility into operational data such as inventory, cash flow, and customer engagement, while the managed service and CI/CD-friendly event-driven design let developers ship features faster. The same foundation helps the company onboard more clients rapidly and treat data-in-motion as a core product differentiator.

solution_components.name: Confluent Cloud
solution_components.role: Runs Pollinate's multi-tenant managed streaming platform for merchant, banking, and product data.

data_flow: Financial and merchant data enters Confluent Cloud through flat files and direct bank streams, flows through Pollinate's microservices on a shared dedicated cluster, and is then used to power onboarding, notifications, and real-time insights for banks and SMB customers.
business_outcome: Pollinate improved operational efficiency, increased developer productivity, enabled faster client onboarding, and delivered richer real-time insights to banking partners and small businesses without expanding platform-management overhead.
architecture_clues: Pollinate operates a multi-tenant platform on a single dedicated Confluent cluster.
The current ingestion model mixes flat files with direct Kafka-based bank integrations.
The event-driven microservices design is tightly integrated with CI/CD workflows for faster feature delivery.
